<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="חשון_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518915147_theRebbe_734" batchId="meluket-_D7_97_D7_A9_D7_95_D7_9F_meluket__BH_POST_1766518915147_theRebbe_734__p002">
  <section v="3">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Yitzchak's blessing "Vayiten Lecha" is loftier than the blessing God gave Yitzchak, which automatically extended to both sons including Esav, whereas Yaakov had to strive for this higher blessing.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">3)</t>
    <t s="1">Now, the blessing with which Yitzchak blessed [Yaakov], "And may God give you," is a blessing more elevated than the blessing of "And God blessed Yitzchak his son."</t>
    <t s="2">For the blessing with which Yitzchak was blessed by God would have been drawn to his children even if he had not blessed them,</t>
    <t s="3">and according to Rashi's commentary on the verse,</t>
    <t s="4">"And God blessed Yitzchak his son" —</t>
    <t s="5">that Avraham was afraid to bless Yitzchak because he foresaw that Esav would descend from him,</t>
    <t s="6">[so] he said, "Let the Master of blessings come and bless whomever is good in His eyes," and the Holy One, blessed be He, came and blessed him.</t>
    <t s="7">From this it is understood</t>
    <t s="8">that just as if Avraham had blessed Yitzchak,</t>
    <t s="9">the blessing would have been drawn also to Esav even if he had not blessed him,</t>
    <t s="10">so too regarding the blessing with which God blessed Yitzchak,</t>
    <t s="11">this blessing was drawn of itself to both his sons,</t>
    <t s="12">even to Esav.</t>
    <t s="13">But the blessing with which Yitzchak blessed [Yaakov], "And may God give you of the dew of the heavens, etc.," is a more elevated blessing.</t>
    <t s="14">And this is also why Yaakov exerted himself greatly and did several things not in his usual manner,</t>
    <t s="15">in order to receive the blessings,</t>
    <t s="16">even though the blessing of "And God blessed Yitzchak his son" was drawn to him of itself,</t>
    <t s="17">because the blessing "And may God give you of the dew of the heavens, etc." is more elevated than the blessing of "And God blessed Yitzchak his son."</t>
  </section>
  <section v="4">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Yitzchak wanted to bless Esav to elevate his lofty holy sparks, but God arranged that Yaakov receive the blessings to properly refine those sparks through him.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">4)</t>
    <t s="1">This will be understood by prefacing what is explained in Torah Ohr on our portion</t>
    <t s="2">and in several discourses,</t>
    <t s="3">that Yitzchak wanted to bless Esav even though he knew that the name of Heaven was not habitual in his mouth,</t>
    <t s="4">because Yitzchak saw that in Esav there were very high holy sparks,</t>
    <t s="5">and therefore he wanted to bless him,</t>
    <t s="6">to draw down upon him a supernal light,</t>
    <t s="7">through which the sparks within him would be refined.</t>
    <t s="8">However,</t>
    <t s="9">if this light had been drawn upon Esav</t>
    <t s="10">(not through Yaakov),</t>
    <t s="11">it would have been in one of two ways —</t>
    <t s="12">either it would have been absorbed within him, or his existence would have been nullified.</t>
    <t s="13">And in order that the refinement of Esav be specifically through Yaakov,</t>
    <t s="14">therefore the Holy One, blessed be He, arranged that Yitzchak would bless Yaakov, and the drawing down of the supernal lights</t>
    <t s="15">(the dew of the heavens and the fat of the land)</t>
    <t s="16">would be to Yaakov,</t>
    <t s="17">through which he would refine the sparks within Esav.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="5">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The aspect of supernal lights that refine the sparks relates to the eleven klipot, whose life-force is separate and counted as an additional entity, unlike holiness where the life-force is internal and unified.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">5)</t>
    <t s="1">And to understand what is the aspect of the supernal lights through which the sparks are refined,</t>
    <t s="2">this will be understood from what is explained in Torah Ohr there and in the aforementioned discourses,</t>
    <t s="3">that the klipot are in number eleven.</t>
    <t s="4">For in holiness the number is ten —</t>
    <t s="5">"ten and not nine, ten and not eleven,"</t>
    <t s="6">but in the side of impurity there are eleven impure crowns.</t>
    <t s="7">And this is also why in the incense there were eleven spices,</t>
    <t s="8">in order to refine the eleven impure crowns.</t>
    <t s="9">And that the side of impurity is in the number eleven</t>
    <t s="10">is</t>
    <t s="11">because they also count the life-force that animates them.</t>
    <t s="12">For in holiness, the life-force of the ten Sefiros</t>
    <t s="13">[and likewise every matter in holiness,</t>
    <t s="14">that every matter is in the number ten]</t>
    <t s="15">is drawn within their inwardness and is unified with them,</t>
    <t s="16">and therefore it is not counted by itself.</t>
    <t s="17">But in the side of impurity,</t>
    <t s="18">the life-force that animates them is separate from them</t>
    <t s="19">[for if it were drawn within them in their inwardness, it would be absorbed within them and would not be an aspect of life-force],</t>
    <t s="20">and therefore it is considered by itself.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
